content: The Corn Poppy, also known as the Field Poppy, Flanders Poppy, or Red Poppy, is a wild poppy species scientifically classified as Papaver rhoeas. It is an annual plant with variable characteristics. The flowers typically have four vivid red petals, often marked with a black spot at their base. In the Northern Hemisphere, the plant usually blooms in late spring, but in warmer climates, additional flowers may appear in early autumn. This plant has been associated with agricultural practices in the Old World since ancient times. It exhibits many traits of a successful agricultural weed, including an annual life cycle that aligns with cereal crops, resistance to basic weed control methods, and the ability to flower and produce seeds before the crop is harvested. Interestingly, like many weeds, it has also been cultivated as a crop in its own right. Its seeds are moderately useful as a commodity, and its flowers are edible. The exact origin of the Corn Poppy is uncertain. Its area of origin is often attributed to Europe by Americans and to Southern Europe by Northern Europeans. The European Garden Flora suggests its native range includes Eurasia and North Africa, regions where agriculture has been practiced since the earliest times. The leaves of the plant are mildly toxic to grazing animals, but the seeds are harmless and are sometimes used as a condiment. The Shirley Poppy, a popular ornamental variety, is derived from forms of this plant. Commonly utilized parts of the Corn Poppy include its seeds (used in baking), fresh green parts (used as a vegetable), and red petals (used to make syrups and both alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages). Red poppy syrup is a traditional drink in Mediterranean regions, such as Bozcaada. Historically, the Corn Poppy has been a symbol of agricultural fertility. In the 20th century, it became strongly associated with wartime remembrance, particularly during Remembrance Day in Commonwealth countries. This association stems from the poppies that bloomed across much of the Western Front during World War I, making them a symbol of military veterans, especially those who served in that war. In Canada, where the poppy is closely tied to Remembrance Day, the Canadian Mint has issued a series of quarters featuring the poppy imprinted at the center of the coin.
